texts: good. the when-clause becomes a rule that can fire, "at night" is kept as the time, and the mist-light is given its own identity in the condition so "the mist-light" in the main clause refers back to it.
good. the whenever version fires the same way, with the night-time trigger, the lantern's showing and the drawing of nightmoths all covered.
good. the denial becomes a rule that reaches any particular nightmoth, and "ordinary firelight" is kept as a firelight that is ordinary, so nothing is dropped.

mixed: the rule itself is right — flying is dialled down to "rarely" and the cold night is kept — but the creature came out under a different symbol here (night_moth) than in your other three sentences (nightmoth), so this fact never joins them. Spell it the same way, with a hyphen, in every sentence: "Night-moths rarely fly on a cold night." One further caveat: the cold night is recorded as part of what rarely happens rather than as a condition, so learning that a night is cold will not by itself make the reasoner expect fewer flights.
